questions.reason: The captured OpenAPI block for the `verbose` query parameter of GET /v1/models reads "type: boolean / default: false / title: Verbose", which establishes `false` as the default; `true`, `1` and `auto` are not defaults of that parameter anywhere on the page.

The overview states verbatim "Unlike traditional containers, Sandboxes supports Git-like branching — fork from any checkpoint, run parallel explorations, and roll back instantly", which is the correct option; OCI images, resource metrics and async operations are listed as separate key features and none is framed as the contrast with containers.

"Key fields to watch during a run" lists "`status`: `validating_files` → `queued` → `running` → `succeeded` / `failed`", so `validating_files` is unambiguously the first status and each distractor is explicitly later in the same chain.

The RerankResult schema documents `relevance_score` with the description "Relevance score of the document", found verbatim; `total_tokens` belongs to RerankUsage ("Total number of tokens used in the request") and `embedding`/`owned_by` do not occur in the rerank response at all.

Step 7 "Download file contents" calls `curl "https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/files/<file_ID>/content"`, while step 6 "Inspect file metadata" uses `/v1/files/<file_ID>` and returns `filename`, `bytes`, `purpose`, so only the `/content` path yields the contents.

The model card list reads "**Quality** — MMLU score reported by the model provider." verbatim, and the three distractors correspond to the separately named "Tokens per second", "Input tokens" and "Output tokens" entries on the same list.

"Minimum replicas are reserved and non-preemptible and remain allocated to your deployment for as long as the endpoint is active" supports the key; the same page releases the allocation when the endpoint stops, confines reclaim risk to scaling above the minimum, and says self-service endpoints have no formal SLA, so no distractor survives.

EmbeddingRequest documents `dimensions` (type integer, examples 4096 and 8192) as "The dimensions to use for the request", found verbatim; `encoding_format` is documented as float or base64 only, and `service_tier`/`model` have no bearing on vector size.

The chat completions response schema says "This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with" and "Can be used in conjunction with the `seed` request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism", both verbatim; the end-user identifier is documented under the separate `user` parameter and token counts under `usage`.

The Quickstart's Third-party integrations card reads "Build inference into applications that are based on supported third-party integrations" verbatim; the Inference, Fine-tuning and API cards each carry the other option texts, and the API card is the path the stem excludes.

The `max_tokens` description states "If omitted or set to null, defaults to 8192 tokens", which rules out the unlimited option; 100 appears only as the parameter's example value and 1 is the documented default of `n`.

"When to use pretokenized datasets" says to use the Pretokenized format if you want to "Have full control over **tokenization, packing, loss masking, and attention masking**", both excerpts verbatim; conversational, instruction and text formats are described purely as `messages`, prompt/completion and `text` shapes with no such control.
